clue.text: Animal has good fair treatment and fine housing

parts.note: G is the usual abbreviation for good

indicators.note: giving something a treatment works it over and changes its form, so the word before it gets rearranged

parts.note: the four letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: a housing is the outer casing of a thing, so only the outside letters of the word before it are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A zoo animal is being looked after well and kept in a decent enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is padding that joins the pieces; 'fine housing' is the shell of the word fine, not a nice enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe is a tall long-necked African mammal, a specific example of a creature.

clue.text: Looked happy going round new church

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the word for happy encloses the other pieces

parts.note: glad means happy
N is the abbreviation for new
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone looked pleased as they walked around a newly built church.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance is to take a brief look, so glanced matches looked as a past tense verb.

clue.text: Charged agent with obstruction and evasion, initially

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative or agent
let is an old word for hindrance, as in without let or hindrance

indicators.note: initially points to the start, so only the opening letter of the word before is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of evasion

explanation.surface: A police report: an agent has been charged with obstructing justice and evading arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' looks like an arrest but means filled up, as a glass is charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Charged can mean loaded or filled to capacity, and replete means full or well supplied.

clue.text: Cast for fine fish

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An angler casts a line hoping for a good fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' sounds like fishing, which fits the surface, but it is a plain verb for throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To fling is to throw something with force, the same act as to cast or hurl.

clue.text: Guessed date and times are wrong

indicators.note: if the letters are wrong they need putting right in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone guessed at the date and the hours and got them wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to make a rough calculation or judgement, so estimated is a synonym for guessed.

clue.text: Wife's rented ragtop punctured and spun noisily

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife; the 's stands for has

indicators.note: something punctured has a thing pushed into it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: rented and hired are synonyms

indicators.note: the top of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of rag is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of rag, the front part of this compound word

explanation.surface: A wife's hired soft-top car gets a puncture and goes spinning off the road with a din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ragtop' looks like one word for a convertible but splits into rag plus top. The R goes inside HIRED, after the W.
explanation.definitionFit: To whirr is to rotate rapidly with a buzzing or humming sound, so the past tense means spun with noise.

clue.text: About half the population has cut back on space

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the word for cut is read from the end

parts.note: to mow is to cut grass
an en is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: Roughly half of the people have had to cut down on room.
explanation.walkthrough: MOW reversed gives WOM; EN is a printing measure of space, half an em.
explanation.definitionFit: Females make up roughly fifty per cent of humanity, a witty description rather than a dictionary synonym.

clue.text: Found popular leader of this South American country's revolution to be losing heart

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the one at its front, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of this

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the country is written backwards
losing its heart means its centre letter drops out

parts.note: Ecuador is a country in South America

explanation.surface: A popular revolutionary leader in a South American country loses his nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: ECUADOR reversed is RODAUCE; dropping its middle letter A leaves RODUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To found a custom or institution is to start or bring it in, which is to introduce it.

clue.text: A semi-virgin oil ruined Italian dish

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: semi means half, so only the first half of the following word is kept

parts.note: the first three of its six letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Using second-rate olive oil spoiled the pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi-virgin' parodies extra virgin olive oil, but it means half of virgin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small square pasta parcels with a filling, a classic dish of Italy.

clue.text: Be entitled to leave — time to go's half five

indicators.note: something told to go must leave, so the time abbreviation is dropped from the word

parts.note: to desert is to leave or abandon
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: half keeps only two of the four letters of the number word

parts.note: the second half of the number word

explanation.surface: A worker's claim to leave work at half past five because it is time to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half five' is British for half past five, but here it is half the word five. DESERT loses T.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve something is to merit it, to have earned the right or claim to it.

clue.text: Choose a parking place

parts.note: taken as written
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a point is a particular place or spot

explanation.surface: An instruction to pick somewhere to leave the car.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint someone is to select or name them for a post, a synonym for choose.

clue.text: Reasons for acting in some ITV play

indicators.note: play suggests loose movement, so the letters of the words before it are allowed to move around

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; ITV is a British television channel

explanation.surface: An actor wonders about a character's motivation in a television drama on ITV, a British commercial channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acting' and 'play' together suggest the theatre, but play is the signal to shuffle the seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Motives are what drive a person to do something, the grounds behind their behaviour.

clue.text: Priest's to run physical training in unpolluted setting

indicators.note: a setting surrounds what sits in it, so the earlier pieces are placed inside the word for unpolluted

parts.note: unpolluted means clean; this is the outer word
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run
gym is short for gymnastics, school physical exercise

explanation.surface: A priest plans to lead an exercise class somewhere with fresh clean air.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for is, and 'to' is padding. 'run' as R comes from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman is a male member of the clergy, and a priest is one such ordained minister.

clue.text: Love party game's retro whiff

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: retro means looking backwards, so the letters for game are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union

explanation.surface: Someone at a party catches the smell of an old-fashioned game.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiff is a faint smell, and an odour is any smell, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Could be a nightmare, when tot swallows drug

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside the swallower, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits, as is a dram
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A nightmare scenario: a small child gets hold of drugs and swallows them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a toddler but is a measure of whisky; E goes inside DRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is one kind of vision during sleep, so the general term is defined by an example.

clue.text: Preserve condition restricting weapon a boy's after

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the condition goes round the following pieces

parts.note: ME is myalgic encephalomyelitis, chronic fatigue syndrome

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first in the run of letters

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearm
taken as written
a lad is a boy; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A boy is after a jar of jam kept out of reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condition' is not a state of repair but the illness chronic fatigue syndrome, abbreviated to its two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus jam, and a preserve is any fruit cooked with sugar to keep.

clue.text: Quite sour cocktail is a shade of blue

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of the words before it are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tart mixed drink turns out to be bright blue, like a blue curacao.
explanation.definitionFit: Turquoise is a greenish-blue colour named after the gemstone, so it is one tint within the blue range.

clue.text: Regret man's 24 hours under energy-blocking routine

indicators.note: in a down clue under means placed lower, so these pieces follow the others
something blocking sits in the way, inside the passage, so the letter goes within the word for routine

parts.note: a rut is a dull fixed routine
E is the physics symbol for energy
he is the pronoun for a man
a day lasts twenty-four hours

explanation.surface: A man regrets spending his whole day stuck in a draining routine.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' means the later pieces come below, that is after, the routine with its energy inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue the day is an idiom meaning to bitterly wish something had never happened.

clue.text: Kind of paper case

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a thick rough drawing paper
second meaning: a casing holding a bullet and its charge, or ink for a printer

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like one description of stationery; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartridge paper is heavy drawing stock, and a cartridge is also a container for ammunition or ink.

clue.text: Report of rogue animal

indicators.note: a report is something heard spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a rogue is a swindler or cheater, said without sounding the final r

explanation.surface: News reaches us of a rogue animal on the loose.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent cheater and the big cat sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is a spotted big cat of Africa, the fastest land mammal, so it is a specific creature.

clue.text: Short cuts for escaping spies?

parts.note: surface reading: quicker routes, side streets drivers use to avoid traffic
setter's reading: a turncoat or informer is a rat, and to run is to escape

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: traitors fleeing take these routes.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain this term means minor residential streets motorists use to bypass congestion, a kind of shortcut.

clue.text: Discharge of English judge by European court

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
J is the abbreviation for judge
E is the abbreviation for European
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A European court dismisses an English judge from office.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject is to throw out or emit forcibly, a synonym for discharge as a verb.

clue.text: Nibble at some meat in tortilla

indicators.note: some means a portion of, so the letters are a run lifted from the following words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: Someone nibbles the filling in a wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat into something is to gradually wear it away, much as nibbling slowly erodes.

clue.text: Drives in and out of American streets

parts.note: thru is the US spelling of through, which means in one side and out the other
St is the abbreviation for street, plural STS

explanation.surface: A motorist drives around the streets of an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drives in and out' looks like the definition, but only Drives is; the rest is through in American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrust is a forceful push, and drives here is the plural noun for powerful forward movements.

clue.text: Special rate covers 10+

indicators.note: a cover goes round what it protects, so the shuffled word goes around the number
a special version is a modified one, so the word after it is altered in order

parts.note: the four letters to be rearranged
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A special price applies to groups of more than ten people.
explanation.walkthrough: The plus sign is the definition, read as a word; ETRA goes round X.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an addition on top of something, and an extra is an additional item or charge.

clue.text: Cushion chair to raise height of Queen behind composer

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the royal abbreviation is placed later in the word than the composer

parts.note: to up something is to raise it
Gustav Holst, English composer of The Planets
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Raising a seat with a cushion so that the Queen sits higher than the composer behind her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cushion' looks like a noun, but with chair it is the verb phrase to pad a seat. Holst wrote The Planets.
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster furniture is to fit it with padding, springs and a fabric covering.

clue.text: Join organisation providing end to poverty

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
providing means on condition that, as if does

indicators.note: an end to a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of poverty

explanation.surface: An appeal to sign up to a charity that will end poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: To unify is to bring things together into one, which is to join or combine them.

clue.text: Left Lincoln with second-class ticket

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
Abraham Lincoln was known as Abe

indicators.note: second picks out the letter in position two of the word that follows

parts.note: the letter in position two of the word

explanation.surface: Someone left the city of Lincoln on a second-class train ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second-class' looks like a ticket grade, but it means the second letter of class.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket is a tag attached to goods showing a price or details, the same as a label.

clue.text: I am nuts swimming in a dangerous wave

indicators.note: things swimming drift about freely, so the letters are moved into new places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A swimmer admits to madness for being out in a huge perilous wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave caused by an earthquake, deadly when it reaches the shore.

clue.text: Daughter's note taking back insult about king proves false

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
E is a note of the musical scale

indicators.note: taking something back returns it the way it came, so the word for insult runs the other way
about means surrounding, so the turned word goes around the abbreviation for king

parts.note: a snub is a slight or insult
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A daughter's letter withdrawing an insult about a king shows a claim was untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: SNUB reversed is BUNS, and K goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To debunk an idea is to expose it as a sham, showing it to be untrue.

clue.text: Chap's coming round, so I straightened line in stockings

indicators.note: coming round means encircling, so the word for chap wraps around the shuffled letters

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

parts.note: the three letters to be rearranged
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A man comes round, and someone straightens the seam on her stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for is; 'line' as railway is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosiery is the collective trade term for socks, tights and similar knitted legwear.

clue.text: Building slowly absorbing earth goes off-white

indicators.note: absorbing means taking something in, so the extra letter joins inside the other word
building puts materials together into a new structure, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for earth

explanation.surface: A building slowly picks up grime and its white paint dulls.
explanation.definitionFit: White paint or paper yellows as it ages, taking on a faded pale tint.
